headline: Dry, mild weather and good travel around Mammoth Lakes and across the Sierra last through Saturday, then rain and high-elevation snow return Sunday into Monday, with a potentially stronger, colder storm bringing winter travel conditions to the Sierra as December begins.

sections.title: Today & Tonight
sections.text: A weakening Pacific storm falls apart as it reaches the Sierra, so Mammoth Lakes and most of the region stay dry; only northeast California north of I-80 could see a few sprinkles or high-elevation flurries through mid-morning, with about a 20 percent chance of a few hundredths of an inch in far western Lassen County. Thick clouds move off to the east Wednesday, allowing a slight warmup with highs in the upper 40s to mid 50s. High thin clouds return Wednesday night, and freezing fog may form again after about midnight around Truckee. No advisories are in effect.

sections.title: Short Term
sections.text: High pressure keeps Thanksgiving through Saturday mainly dry with periods of high thin clouds and favorable travel across the Sierra and western Nevada. Patchy freezing fog is likely each morning before 9 AM along I-80 near Truckee and the Martis Valley (60 to 80 percent chance at Truckee), and cold air trapped in the valleys may bring hazy mornings around Reno, Carson City and Minden. Afternoons warm above late-November averages, with highs mainly in the 50s to near 60 in the lower elevations and Sierra communities. Far northeastern California and northwestern Nevada north of Susanville and Gerlach have a 15 to 25 percent chance of light rain showers Friday night.

sections.title: Long Term
sections.text: A more active storm pattern returns Sunday, with rain, higher-elevation snow and gusty winds Sunday into Monday, most likely Sunday afternoon and evening (50 to 90 percent chance in the Sierra and northeast California, 20 to 60 percent in western Nevada). This storm is fairly mild, with snow levels near or above 7,000 to 7,500 feet, but snow could still affect the higher Sierra passes, so allow extra time for travel home after the holiday weekend. More storms are lined up for the first days of December and look likely to bring bigger impacts, with snow levels mostly 5,500 to 6,500 feet and some colder scenarios down to 4,500 to 5,000 feet, so plan for winter driving conditions in the Sierra next week.

watch_for: Snow on the higher Sierra passes Sunday afternoon and evening during return holiday travel
Timing and amounts for the early-December storms, which could bring lower snow levels
Morning freezing fog along I-80 near Truckee through Saturday
confidence: Confidence is high in dry weather through Saturday and fairly good for the Sunday–Monday storm, but forecast models still disagree on the timing and amounts of the early-December storms.
